properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14:

"I'm curious if we can use flo2 to solve: navier Stokes: https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/ and https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openais-blockbuster-navier-stokes-proof-isnt-what-we-thought-it-was/. However instead of using a complete reasoning model to compute proof, if we could instead use reflow2 to record equations (maybe need flo2-calc) and the reasoning of opus 5.5 to put the proof together"

The two articles were NOT read. His brainstorm rule is "don't start building or researching", so nothing here says what they report. The trial target, Navier–Stokes, is recorded separately: dec:idea-navier-stokes-as-a-trial-of-designing-a-proof.

WHAT IS ALREADY RECORDED, so this revisits a question rather than opening a new one:
- flo2-calc's design, dec:idea-flo2-calc-builds-and-checks-a-proof (settled 2026-10-04). He asked there for "design me a proof of some mathematical expression", then reframed it: "maybe a proof is too advanced for now". He chose (g) designing a study's math up front and (j) a served skill for it. Kept as considered: (c) checked derivations, (d) symbolic equivalence and (e) a proof-assistant helper (Lean 4 with mathlib). This idea revisits (c) and (e). The choice of (g) and (j) stands.
- dec:idea-reflow2-designs-a-line-of-reasoning-an-argument-an-experiment-a-paper-a-legal-case (open, 2026-10-14). A proof is the most exacting line of reasoning there is.

HOW A PROOF MAPS onto what exists (a sketch to test, not a rule):
- the theorem → a Requirement ("what must be shown");
- its hypotheses and the function spaces it lives in → Constraints;
- lemmas → parts, each allocated the claims it must establish; the dependency between lemmas → DEPENDS_ON;
- the proof strategy → a Decision with its alternatives (for example energy estimates or a blow-up construction);
- each step's justification → a Verification, whose kind says WHO checked it: a machine (proof assistant), a person (a named mathematician) or nobody (a model's narration);
- known obstructions and counterexamples → RISKS and CONTRADICTS.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) STRUCTURE ONLY. The mapping above, written in a design, with every step marked by who checked it. No build.
(b) EQUATIONS ON THE NODES. Each step carries its equation as data, and flo2-calc evaluates what can be evaluated: units, special cases, numerical spot checks. This is evidence, not proof.
(c) CHECKED DERIVATION STEPS in flo2-calc: the model proposes each step and a rule checker verifies it (flo2-calc's option (c)).
(d) A PROOF-ASSISTANT HELPER (Lean 4 with mathlib), standalone. Each lemma node links to a machine-checked proof, and reflow2 shows which lemmas are checked and which are still narrated (flo2-calc's option (e)).
(e) VALIDATED NUMERICS: interval arithmetic with rigorous rounding, so a computation can be one step of a computer-assisted proof. As I recall, without checking: computer-assisted proofs of blow-up for the related Euler equations have been done this way (Chen and Hou, 2022).
(f) A SERVED "DESIGN A PROOF" SKILL that walks an agent and a person through (a), and points at (b) to (e) where they exist.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- RECORDING IS NOT REASONING. reflow2 adds no proving power. The insight still has to come from somewhere, and Opus is itself a reasoning model. What the design adds is the AUDIT: every step's dependencies, assumptions and checker are visible, so a gap shows as a gap. That is what separates a proof from one that "isn't what we thought it was".
- ONLY A CHECKER MAKES A STEP PROVEN. A step counts as proven when a proof assistant's kernel or a qualified mathematician has checked it. A model narrating it does not count. The design must never read a narrated step as proven. STRUCTURE IS NOT TRUTH (job 3 of dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well): a well-connected proof graph can LOOK finished.
- EVALUATING IS NOT PROVING, already recorded on flo2-calc's decision. Numbers at many points are evidence. For a statement about all solutions at all times, numerics alone settle nothing, except as a rigorous computer-assisted step under (e).
- FORMALIZATION REACH, my understanding and unverified: the analysis a PDE regularity proof needs (Sobolev spaces, energy estimates, regularity theory) is far from what Lean's library holds today. So (d) for a hard PDE result means formalizing large parts of analysis first.
- IT CAME FROM READING. rule:an-idea-from-reading-waits-for-a-real-use-before-it-is-built (advisory, 2026-10-13) says the default is to wait for a real use. Real uses of the same machinery already on the record: his thesis methodology (flo2-calc's (g)) and Chris's argument.

SIZE, plainly (a finding, not a decision):
- (a): no build, only how a design is written.
- (f): small, skill text.
- (b): small to moderate, since flo2-calc has the operators and units.
- (c): large, a rule set and a step checker.
- (d): large, a separate helper with a heavy library, and much larger again for PDE analysis.
- (e): large, rigorous interval arithmetic throughout flo2-calc.

2026-10-14, LATER: ANTHONY CORRECTS THE FRAMING. Still brainstorming.

IN HIS WORDS: "this isn't using flo2-calc to do the proof. This is designing a hypothesis for the proof using reflow2, captured in the graph, then going through systematically, and step by step comptuing the proof"

So the idea is reflow2's own loop, applied to a proof: DESIGN FIRST, THEN BUILD ONLY WHAT THE GRAPH SPECIFIES. flo2-calc is not the prover. At most it keeps an equation's record, which is why the options above ranked it too prominently. Options (b) to (e) above are now only ways to STRENGTHEN ONE STEP'S CHECK, not the method.

THE METHOD, as he describes it:
(g) THE PROOF AS A DESIGN-THEN-BUILD LOOP.
  - DESIGN: the theorem is the Requirement. The hypothesis for the proof (the strategy) is a Decision with its alternatives. The lemmas it needs are decomposed beneath it, each with DEPENDS_ON to what it rests on and its assumptions as Constraints. All of this is captured before any step is worked.
  - BUILD: Opus takes the open lemmas in dependency order, the way what_next and frontier pick the next buildable piece. It works each step and records the argument with its status, and the graph shows what that step unlocks.
  - A FAILED ATTEMPT is recorded with why it failed, so no later session retries it blind. propagate_change shows everything that rested on a lemma that fell.
(h) EACH STEP REVIEWED BY A SECOND, INDEPENDENT AGENT before it counts as done: the owner/designer/observer pattern of the three-agent trials. A model's review is not proof, but it catches the slips a single reasoner makes.

WHAT THE GRAPH IS GENUINELY GOOD FOR HERE (a finding):
- CONTINUITY. A hard proof outlasts any one session or context window. The graph holds the plan, what is done, what failed and why, across sessions and across models. That is job 1 of dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well.
- DEPENDENCY. It shows which results rest on which lemmas, and what breaks when one fails.
- DEAD ENDS KEPT, so the same wrong road is not walked twice.

PUSHBACK, UPDATED for this framing:
- THE HARD PART IS THE HYPOTHESIS. A wrong strategy is found only deep into the build. The graph does not make the plan right. It makes a wrong plan cheap to see and cheap to abandon when a lemma fails.
- "COMPUTING" A STEP IS REASONING, NOT ARITHMETIC. A step the model marks done can still be wrong. What upgrades "done" to "checked" is (h), a person, or a proof checker ((d) above). The design must show which one each step has.
- The earlier pushback stands: structure is not truth, and the idea came from reading.

SIZE: (g) needs no engine build. It is a way of writing a design plus a served skill for it, so it is small. (h) is small: it is how the trials already run.

2026-10-14, LATER: ANTHONY SHARPENS THE IDEA. Still brainstorming.

IN HIS WORDS:
- "this isn't using flo2-calc to do the proof. This is designing a hypothesis for the proof using reflow2, captured in the graph, then going through systematically, and step by step comptuing the proof"
- "your \"design a proof\" is what I'm getting at (though just using reflow2 natively, not a new skill). The design graph becomes the proof, if that makes sense - assuming that the reflow2 has the nodes and edges for this."
- "Basically, the reflow2 design graph is the mathematical proof in graph form is what I'm thinking about"

His picture: Premise 1 (P) and Premise 2 (P → Q) both feed an Operation node (Modus Ponens), which yields the Conclusion (Q).

FROM THE TEXT HE PASTED, the fields where a graph IS the proof:
- proof nets (Girard, linear logic): a graph of formulas that is a valid proof when it meets a correctness criterion;
- deep inference and the calculus of structures;
- combinatorial proofs. The pasted text credits Hetzl and Heijltjes; as I recall they are Dominic Hughes's ("Proofs Without Syntax", 2006), with Heijltjes and Straßburger on the intuitionistic case. Unchecked.
- proofs as DAGs of statements and inference steps (Curry–Howard: a proof is a program), and syntax trees;
- Peirce's existential graphs, and string diagrams in category theory.
The pasted text also says automated theorem provers were used in OpenAI's Navier–Stokes verification. That was NOT checked.

SO THE IDEA IS: the design graph IS the proof, built with reflow2 natively, with no new skill and no flo2-calc. Statements are nodes, inference steps are nodes, and edges carry the deductions. The hypothesis is designed first, then worked through step by step.

WHAT reflow2's VOCABULARY HAS TODAY (a finding, measured with describe_schema on reflow2's design: 28 node types, 66 edge types):
- STATEMENTS FIT:
  - the theorem and its lemmas as Requirements; lineage `derived` exists, and status `met` can mean shown;
  - hypotheses and axioms as Constraints;
  - the theorem split into lemmas with DECOMPOSES;
  - a conclusion DEPENDS_ON its premises;
  - a counterexample CONTRADICTS a claim.
- MISSING:
  (1) NO NODE FOR THE OPERATION, the middle box of his picture: an inference rule applied (modus ponens, induction, an estimate). The nearest fits are poor. A Verification with method `analysis` cannot VERIFY a Requirement (VERIFIES reaches Artifact, Capability, Component and Constraint). A Decision means a choice, not a deduction.
  (2) NO EDGE THAT MEANS "follows from, by rule R". DEPENDS_ON carries the dependency, but its dependency_type values are software's (function_call, data_flow, control_flow, error_flow, physical), so the rule would live in free text.
  (3) NOTHING CHECKS THAT A STEP FOLLOWS. Statements are prose, and no computation reads them as logic. reflow2's checks are structural, such as whether every claim has premises. Not checked: whether a DEPENDS_ON cycle among requirements (circular reasoning) is flagged.

NEW OPTIONS for this framing:
(g) NATIVE, AS IS: statements and dependencies mapped onto the types above, each step's rule named in the edge's note. No build. The operation lives in the edge rather than as a node, and gaps (1) and (2) are carried in prose.
(h) A SMALL VOCABULARY ADDITION: an inference-step node (its rule, premises in, conclusion out), and an edge or a dependency_type value meaning "follows from". This is option (d) of dec:idea-reflow2-designs-a-line-of-reasoning-an-argument-an-experiment-a-paper-a-legal-case. Its objection there was that it fails the "fewer things" yardstick. Shared by proofs, arguments, legal cases and experiments, that objection is weaker.
(i) STATEMENTS WRITTEN IN A FORMAL LANGUAGE on the nodes (Lean, or a first-order syntax), so that a checker CAN read each step. This joins option (d) above, the proof-assistant helper.

PUSHBACK, UPDATED:
- A GRAPH OF A PROOF IS A PROOF ONLY IF ITS STEPS ARE CHECKED. Every field he cites has a correctness criterion, or rules applied mechanically to each step. reflow2 can hold the graph and show what rests on what. It cannot today judge that Q follows from P and P → Q. Without that, the design is a proof's outline with its dependencies: valuable, but not yet a proof.
- The earlier pushback stands: structure is not truth, and the idea came from reading.

SIZE (a finding): (g) is no build. (h) is small to moderate: a schema change served to every design. (i) is large.
